title: Private-network URL access is blocked
summary: Fetch and browser surfaces cannot reach private, loopback or cloud-metadata addresses unless explicitly required.

protected.asset: Internal services and metadata endpoints reachable from the deployment
protected.failure: Instructed content makes the agent probe or use internal endpoints as an exfiltration or pivot path.

rationale: Wherever the deployment can follow URLs, private-address access is a pivot into the surrounding network. The default posture is blocked, with any exception an explicit, reviewed allowance. Missing browser or deployment facts leave applicability undecided, never silently safe.

variants.description: Set every private-URL access setting the build exposes to disabled, including automatic local fallbacks, per home.
Config denial plus an egress rule that blocks private ranges at the network layer, covering tools that ignore configuration.

verification.method: Read each private-URL setting back per home, then run harmless deny and allow probes against a private address that must not be fetched.
verification.evidence: Setting names and read-back values plus probe outcomes; no internal address details beyond the fact that access was denied.

rollback.method: Restore previous per-home values; remove the egress exception only after confirming no legitimate private fetch depends on it.

failure_modes: A sparse named profile inherits a permissive built-in default for an access leaf.
An automatic local fallback re-enables private access even with the main switch off.
Egress rules cover one tool family while another resolves private names freely.

hermes_versions.notes: Synthetic seed control: the range is an illustrative placeholder for the example registry, not a verified compatibility claim.
